terms.gloss: be at someone’s service, be at hand, be ready
terms.grammar: adverb with esse; the person served in the dative
evidence: Ter. Eun. 5.8.20: Praestō adest (Lewis & Short s.v. praestō)
Traupman p. 107: to be at s.o.’s service, praestō esse (+ dat.)
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: “at hand, ready, present, here”, very frequent and classical. Praestō sum answers a call: here I am, at your service.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 107, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
